system:
You are the analysis agent of a reporting platform for Australia's threatened species. Conservation practitioners — people in government agencies, NGOs and recovery teams who decide where to survey, what to protect and what to escalate — read what you produce. You have read-only SQL access to the platform's database and produce insights from it, each grounded in queries you ran.

# The data

PostgreSQL 17 with PostGIS 3.5. The corpus is every occurrence record the Atlas of Living Australia (ALA) tags as nationally threatened (EPBC Critically Endangered, Endangered or Vulnerable), observed January 2015 to 2026-09-30, from one bulk download (DOI 10.26197/ala.40eee344-07ce-48d2-9ec2-be39574ff4c7): about 2.1 million records, 1,850 taxa, 300+ contributing datasets. Alongside it are all-taxa effort counts per 0.1° cell per month for the same period.

corpus.analysable_occurrences — VIEW — the records to analyse: occurrences that are valid, dated, and not from telemetry (animal-tracking) datasets. Includes population ('wild' or 'managed' — managed means a fenced haven, reintroduction or other managed population, set from the dataset or from corpus.managed_populations) and dataset_kind (the dataset's own kind). Prefer this over occurrences.
  columns: record_id text, source text, source_record_id text, occurrence_id text, harvest_id text, snapshot_page text, fetched_at timestamp with time zone, data_resource_uid text, license text, taxon_concept_id text, scientific_name text, vernacular_name text, national_status text, event_date timestamp with time zone, first_loaded_at timestamp with time zone, decimal_latitude double precision, decimal_longitude double precision, coordinate_uncertainty_m double precision, state_province text, ibra_region text, locality text, geom USER-DEFINED, basis_of_record text, individual_count integer, recorded_by_pseudonym text, source_assertions ARRAY, is_valid boolean, issue_count integer, cell_lat numeric, cell_lon numeric, event_day date, managed_by_rule boolean, dataset_kind text, population text

corpus.datasets — TABLE — contributing datasets; kind is 'wild', 'managed' (fenced havens, reintroductions) or 'telemetry' (excluded from analysable_occurrences).
  columns: data_resource_uid text, name text, kind text, kind_reason text, first_seen_at timestamp with time zone

corpus.effort_cells — TABLE — record counts (threatened or not, telemetry excluded) per 0.1° cell per month, per taxon_group: 'all' (every taxon), or 'Aves', 'Mammalia', 'Reptilia', 'Amphibia', 'Plantae' (that group only). The denominator for reporting rates. Join on cell_lat/cell_lon and month, and always filter taxon_group — summing across groups double-counts.
  columns: cell_lat numeric, cell_lon numeric, period_start date, period_end date, records integer, harvest_id text, taxon_group text

corpus.harvest_runs — TABLE — provenance of each harvest (the corpus download and the effort counts).
  columns: harvest_id text, harvest_key text, run_id text, source text, description text, query jsonb, started_at timestamp with time zone, finished_at timestamp with time zone, expected_records integer, retrieved_records integer, complete boolean, corpus_hash text, request_count integer, warnings jsonb, analysis jsonb, loaded_at timestamp with time zone

corpus.managed_populations — TABLE — curated rules marking managed populations: a taxon in a state (optionally narrowed to an IBRA region and a dataset), e.g. Bilby in NSW, where it survives only in fenced havens, or Woylie in AWC's Mt Gibson haven. Already applied in analysable_occurrences.population.
  columns: taxon_concept_id text, state_province text, note text, rule_id integer, ibra_region text, data_resource_uid text

corpus.occurrences — TABLE — every canonical occurrence record, telemetry included. event_date is the observation instant (timestamptz); event_day is its Australian Eastern local date. geom is a PostGIS Point (SRID 4326); cell_lat/cell_lon are the 0.1° grid cell (rounded to nearest, as ALA assigns them).
  columns: record_id text, source text, source_record_id text, occurrence_id text, harvest_id text, snapshot_page text, fetched_at timestamp with time zone, data_resource_uid text, license text, taxon_concept_id text, scientific_name text, vernacular_name text, national_status text, event_date timestamp with time zone, first_loaded_at timestamp with time zone, decimal_latitude double precision, decimal_longitude double precision, coordinate_uncertainty_m double precision, state_province text, ibra_region text, locality text, geom USER-DEFINED, basis_of_record text, individual_count integer, recorded_by_pseudonym text, source_assertions ARRAY, is_valid boolean, issue_count integer, cell_lat numeric, cell_lon numeric, event_day date, managed_by_rule boolean

corpus.taxa — TABLE — one row per taxon (key taxon_concept_id); national_status is the EPBC status ALA attached.
  columns: taxon_concept_id text, scientific_name text, vernacular_name text, taxon_rank text, kingdom text, phylum text, taxon_class text, taxon_order text, family text, genus text, national_status text, status_seen_at timestamp with time zone

corpus.taxon_tiers — VIEW — per taxon: analysable records since 2015, last_record_day, and statistical_tier (≥100 records since 2015).
  columns: taxon_concept_id text, scientific_name text, vernacular_name text, national_status text, records_since_2015 bigint, last_record_day date, statistical_tier boolean

Useful facts: EPSG:3577 (Australian Albers, equal-area, metres) is available for gridding and areas; ibra_region is the IBRA 7 bioregion (null offshore — IBRA covers land only); coordinate_uncertainty_m is the radius the true position may lie within.

**Dates: use event_day** (the Australian Eastern local date) for every date window, count by period and date you report — not event_date, which is an instant stored in UTC and would put early-morning Australian records on the previous day.

# Known properties of this data — read before interpreting anything

- **Records measure effort as much as animals.** These are mostly opportunistic records. All-taxa recording roughly doubled between 2017–19 and 2022–24 (about 1.9×), so counts and range measures grow with effort. Use corpus.effort_cells as a denominator where it matters.
- **Recent months are incomplete.** Datasets reach ALA months to a year late: January–August 2026 holds about 20% of the records January–August 2024 holds, and eBird (the largest dataset) has not loaded 2026 at all. A recent decline is not evidence of anything until this is accounted for.
- **Sources start and stop.** A compilation that ends in 2020, or a targeted survey wound up inside an ongoing state atlas, looks exactly like range loss. Check which datasets carry a taxon's records in each period before calling a change real.
- **Locations vary in precision.** About half the analysable records are located to within 2 km; about a third state no uncertainty; ALA generalises many sensitive species to roughly 10 km.
- **Managed populations** (population = 'managed': fenced havens, reintroductions) are in the analysable view and are not wild trend.
- **National status** is as ALA attached it. Never infer, change or second-guess a taxon's conservation status.
- Taxonomy can shift: a taxon "disappearing" from a region can be a name re-assignment.

# How to work

- Call run_sql with one SELECT (or WITH … SELECT) per call, no trailing statements. Results are capped at 200 rows and queries time out after 30 s, so aggregate in SQL rather than pulling rows. Each call returns a query_id.
- Record each insight with record_insight as soon as it is established. Every insight cites the query_ids whose results support it, and every number in it must be a value those queries returned or simple arithmetic on them. Do not state figures you did not query.
- taxon_concept_id must be copied exactly from corpus.taxa; when an insight is about several taxa, put the main one there (or null) and list the others in related_taxa; region is an IBRA region name exactly as in ibra_region, or null for a national insight; period_start and period_end are the window the insight describes.
- Say how confident you are and why, in the confidence field: record counts, the datasets involved, effort, precision, and any artefact that could explain the pattern.
- When you have recorded everything worth recording, stop.

tools.description: Run one read-only SQL query (a single SELECT or WITH … SELECT) against the corpus. Returns a query_id, the columns and up to 200 rows. Cite the query_id in any insight that relies on the result.

sql.description: One SELECT or WITH … SELECT statement.

purpose.description: One line: what this query is for.

tools.name: record_insight
tools.description: Record one insight. Every figure must come from the cited queries.

related_taxa.description: Optional: other taxon_concept_ids this insight is about, exactly as in corpus.taxa.

region.description: IBRA region name exactly as in ibra_region, or null for national.

period_start.description: YYYY-MM-DD — start of the window the insight describes.

figures.description: The numbers behind the insight, as returned by your queries.

confidence.description: Why this should or should not be trusted: records, datasets, effort, precision, possible artefacts.

summary.description: One or two sentences a practitioner can act on.

query_ids.description: The run_sql query_ids whose results support this insight.

messages.content:
Report month: 2026-09 (2026-09-01 to 2026-09-30). Compute the five insights below exactly as defined and record them with record_insight, using the insight_type given. "Analysable" means corpus.analysable_occurrences. The statistical tier is taxa with statistical_tier = true in corpus.taxon_tiers.

## 1. silent_species — period 2023-10-01 to 2026-09-30
(a) Silent: taxa in corpus.taxa with no analysable record in that window (whatever their record count).
(b) Evidence gap: taxa with fewer than 10 analysable records since 2015.
(c) Regional silence: a taxon and IBRA region where the taxon had at least 5 analysable records in 2015–2019 but none in the window, while the taxon was still recorded nationally in the window.
Record one headline insight per kind (taxon and region null; figures {kind: "silent" | "evidence_gap" | "regional_silence", count}), then individual insights for the most important cases, up to 15 per kind (figures {kind, last_record_date, records_since_2015, …}, last_record_date as event_day; regional ones with region set).

## 2. range_change — statistical tier, 2017–2019 against 2022–2024 (period 2022-01-01 to 2024-12-31)
Per taxon and window, from analysable records with coordinates:
Wild records only (population = 'wild').
- AOO 10 km: distinct 10 km cells on an EPSG:3577 grid, all records; area = cells × 100 km².
- AOO 2 km: distinct 2 km cells, only records with coordinate_uncertainty_m ≤ 2000; area = cells × 4 km².
- EOO: area of the convex hull of all records, km².
Flag "contraction" or "expansion" when the 10 km AOO changes by at least 30% and both windows have at least 20 records.
Record headline insights with the count of contractions and of expansions (figures {flag, count}), then individual insights for the most important flagged taxa, up to 15 (figures {flag, aoo_10km_km2: {baseline, recent, change}, aoo_2km_km2: {baseline, recent, change}, eoo_km2: {baseline, recent, change}, records: {baseline, recent}}, change as a fraction).

## 3. notable_record — records in 2026-09 of statistical-tier taxa
A record is notable if it is more than 100 km from every earlier analysable record of the taxon (since 2015), or in an IBRA region with no earlier record of the taxon, or in a calendar month holding less than 1% of the taxon's 2015–2019 records (judged only where the taxon has at least 100 such records). Group by taxon and IBRA region: one insight per group, up to 30 (figures {reasons: [...], records, max_distance_to_prior_km}, reasons drawn from "outside_range", "new_region", "out_of_season").

## 4. reporting_rate — statistical tier, 2017–2019 against 2022–2024 (period 2022-01-01 to 2024-12-31)
Wild analysable records with a grid cell (cell_lat not null), per taxon, nationally and per IBRA region.
- Effort group: 'Plantae' if the taxon's kingdom is Plantae; its taxon_class if Aves, Mammalia, Reptilia or Amphibia; otherwise 'all'.
- Footprint: the 0.1° cells where the taxon (in that region, for a regional figure) has a record in either window.
- Consistent sources: datasets that recorded the taxon (in that scope) in both windows. Both numerators below count only their records.
- Detection ratio (the flag): per window, detections = distinct (cell, month of event_day) in the footprint with a consistent-source record; visits = footprint cell-months with effort_cells records > 0 for the effort group; rate = detections ÷ visits; ratio = recent rate ÷ baseline rate. 95% interval: ratio × exp(±1.96 × √(1/d_baseline − 1/v_baseline + 1/d_recent − 1/v_recent)).
- Record ratio: per window, consistent-source records ÷ effort-group records summed over the footprint cells and the window's months; ratio = recent ÷ baseline.
Flag "decline" when the detection ratio is ≤ 0.7, its interval's upper end is below 1 and the record ratio is below 1; "increase" when the detection ratio is ≥ 1.4286, its interval's lower end is above 1 and the record ratio is above 1; both need at least 20 detections in each window. Regional figures only for taxon–region pairs with at least 20 records (all sources) in each window.
Record national headline insights with the count of declines and of increases (taxon and region null; figures {flag, count}), then individual insights for the most important flagged taxa, nationally and by region, up to 15 each (figures {flag, effort_group, detections: {baseline, recent}, visits: {baseline, recent}, detection_ratio, detection_ratio_ci95: [low, high], consistent_source_ratio}).

## 5. co_movement — IBRA regions, from section 4's regional results (period 2022-01-01 to 2024-12-31)
A taxon–region pair is assessed when section 4 gives it at least 20 detections in each window. Per region: taxa_assessed, declines and increases (section 4 flags). Expected shares: the share of all assessed taxon–region pairs, nationally, flagged decline (and increase). p_decline = P(X ≥ declines) for X ~ Binomial(taxa_assessed, expected decline share); p_increase likewise. Flag "co_decline" when declines ≥ 3 and p_decline < 0.05; otherwise "co_increase" when increases ≥ 3 and p_increase < 0.05.
Record headline insights with the count of co_decline and of co_increase regions (taxon and region null; figures {flag, count}), then one insight per flagged region (region set, taxon null, related_taxa = the taxa that moved; figures {flag, taxa_assessed, declines, increases, p_decline, p_increase}).

Beyond these, record anything else a practitioner should know as insight_type "other".

input.sql: SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM corpus.taxa) taxa, (SELECT count(*) FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences) recs, (SELECT max(event_day) FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences) maxday, (SELECT count(*) FROM corpus.taxon_tiers WHERE statistical_tier) tier

WITH w AS (SELECT DISTINCT taxon_concept_id FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences WHERE event_day BETWEEN '2023-10-01' AND '2026-09-30'),
s AS (SELECT t.taxon_concept_id FROM corpus.taxa t WHERE t.taxon_concept_id NOT IN (SELECT taxon_concept_id FROM w)),
g AS (SELECT t.taxon_concept_id FROM corpus.taxa t LEFT JOIN corpus.taxon_tiers tt USING (taxon_concept_id) WHERE coalesce(tt.records_since_2015,0) < 10)
SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM s) silent, (SELECT count(*) FROM g) gap, (SELECT count(*) FROM s WHERE taxon_concept_id IN (SELECT taxon_concept_id FROM g)) both_,
(SELECT count(*) FROM s JOIN corpus.taxon_tiers tt USING (taxon_concept_id) WHERE tt.records_since_2015>0) silent_with_records

WITH b AS (SELECT taxon_concept_id, ibra_region, count(*) n, max(event_day) lastb FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences WHERE event_day BETWEEN '2015-01-01' AND '2019-12-31' AND ibra_region IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING count(*)>=5),
w AS (SELECT DISTINCT taxon_concept_id, ibra_region FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences WHERE event_day BETWEEN '2023-10-01' AND '2026-09-30'),
nat AS (SELECT DISTINCT taxon_concept_id FROM w)
SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT b.taxon_concept_id) FROM b WHERE b.taxon_concept_id IN (SELECT taxon_concept_id FROM nat) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM w WHERE w.taxon_concept_id=b.taxon_concept_id AND w.ibra_region=b.ibra_region)
SELECT count(*) FROM corpus.taxon_tiers

WITH w AS (SELECT DISTINCT taxon_concept_id FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences WHERE event_day BETWEEN '2023-10-01' AND '2026-09-30')
SELECT tt.taxon_concept_id, tt.scientific_name, tt.vernacular_name, tt.national_status, tt.records_since_2015, tt.last_record_day::text,
 (SELECT count(DISTINCT data_resource_uid) FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences a WHERE a.taxon_concept_id=tt.taxon_concept_id) nds,
 (SELECT count(*) FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences a WHERE a.taxon_concept_id=tt.taxon_concept_id AND population='managed') managed,
 (SELECT count(*) FROM corpus.occurrences o WHERE o.taxon_concept_id=tt.taxon_concept_id AND o.event_day>='2023-10-01') any_occ_window
FROM corpus.taxon_tiers tt WHERE tt.taxon_concept_id NOT IN (SELECT taxon_concept_id FROM w)
ORDER BY tt.records_since_2015 DESC LIMIT 30

WITH b AS (SELECT taxon_concept_id, ibra_region, count(*) n FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences WHERE event_day BETWEEN '2015-01-01' AND '2019-12-31' AND ibra_region IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING count(*)>=5),
w AS (SELECT DISTINCT taxon_concept_id, ibra_region FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences WHERE event_day BETWEEN '2023-10-01' AND '2026-09-30'),
nat AS (SELECT taxon_concept_id, count(*) nw FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences WHERE event_day BETWEEN '2023-10-01' AND '2026-09-30' GROUP BY 1),
rs AS (SELECT b.*, nat.nw FROM b JOIN nat USING (taxon_concept_id) WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM w WHERE w.taxon_concept_id=b.taxon_concept_id AND w.ibra_region=b.ibra_region))
SELECT rs.taxon_concept_id, t.scientific_name, t.vernacular_name, t.national_status, rs.ibra_region, rs.n n1519, rs.nw nat_window,
 count(a.*) since2015, max(a.event_day)::text lastday, count(DISTINCT a.data_resource_uid) nds, sum(CASE WHEN a.population='managed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) managed,
 (array_agg(d.name ORDER BY d.name))[1] ds1
FROM rs JOIN corpus.taxa t USING (taxon_concept_id) JOIN corpus.analysable_occurrences a ON a.taxon_concept_id=rs.taxon_concept_id AND a.ibra_region=rs.ibra_region JOIN corpus.datasets d ON d.data_resource_uid=a.data_resource_uid
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5,6,7 ORDER BY rs.n DESC LIMIT 40

w AS (SELECT DISTINCT taxon_concept_id, ibra_region FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences WHERE event_day BETWEEN '2023-10-01' AND '2026-09-30'),

x AS (SELECT a.taxon_concept_id, a.ibra_region, count(*) since2015, max(a.event_day) lastday, count(DISTINCT a.data_resource_uid) nds, sum(CASE WHEN a.population='managed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) managed, min(a.data_resource_uid) ds1
 FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences a JOIN rs ON a.taxon_concept_id=rs.taxon_concept_id AND a.ibra_region=rs.ibra_region GROUP BY 1,2)
SELECT rs.taxon_concept_id, t.scientific_name, t.vernacular_name, t.national_status, rs.ibra_region, rs.n n1519, rs.nw nat_window, x.since2015, x.lastday::text, x.nds, x.managed, d.name
FROM rs JOIN corpus.taxa t USING (taxon_concept_id) JOIN x ON x.taxon_concept_id=rs.taxon_concept_id AND x.ibra_region=rs.ibra_region LEFT JOIN corpus.datasets d ON d.data_resource_uid=x.ds1
ORDER BY rs.n DESC LIMIT 40

input.summary: 35 statistical-tier taxa lost at least 30% of their 10 km AOO between 2017–19 and 2022–24, even though overall recording effort roughly doubled. Most of the largest contractions follow a dataset ending rather than a confirmed loss.

confidence.level: low as evidence of real spread
confidence.notes: All-taxa recording rose about 1.9× between the windows, and AOO is not effort-corrected, so most expansions are expected from effort alone. Use section 4's reporting rates for effort-adjusted change.

input.summary: 228 statistical-tier taxa gained at least 30% in 10 km AOO, against 35 contractions. Most of the gain reflects the doubling in recording effort rather than real spread, so do not use these as evidence of recovery without checking effort.

confidence.notes: Record numbers held steady (1,352 to 1,203), so this is not just less recording. However, the source mix changed: VBA contributed 493 baseline records and none recent, and eBird rose from 285 to 792 records generalised to about 10 km. Records concentrating at a few known sites, or Victorian records not loading, could explain part of it. The 2 km AOO is unreliable because most records are generalised.

input.summary: Regent Honeyeater (Critically Endangered) records cover about half the 10 km cells they did (12,600 to 6,400 km²) and its EOO fell 78%, on a similar number of records. Its recent records come from far fewer places. Check whether the missing Victorian (VBA) records reflect the bird or the data feed.

confidence.level: low as evidence of range loss
confidence.notes: 747 of 774 baseline records come from the NESP A12 compilation, which ends in 2020. Recent records are mostly 11 museum specimens. This is a source artefact.

input.summary: Pacific Ridley turtle (Endangered) shows a 95% fall in 10 km AOO, but almost all baseline records come from a NESP compilation that ended in 2020. ALA now has almost no monitoring data on this turtle, which is a data gap to fill rather than a confirmed decline.

confidence.level: low as evidence of range loss
confidence.notes: Baseline records come from Kimberley survey datasets (2004–2020), NESP A12 and Fauna Atlas N.T., all ended or inactive. Recent records are 18 iNaturalist sightings. This is a source artefact.

input.summary: Australian Snubfin Dolphin (Vulnerable) shows an 84% fall in 10 km AOO, driven by survey datasets that ended in 2020. ALA has no ongoing systematic monitoring of it, so ask WA and NT agencies for current survey data.

confidence.level: low as evidence of range loss
confidence.notes: 6,138 of 6,204 baseline records come from Fauna Atlas N.T., which contributed only 24 recent records. EOO and 2 km AOO both rose, so the contraction is a source artefact.

input.summary: Northern Brushtail Possum (Vulnerable) is flagged as a contraction (10 km AOO −55%), but this comes from Fauna Atlas N.T. dropping out. EOO actually grew by 48%. Monitoring has no current data stream for it.

confidence.notes: 1,140 baseline records come from the ACT Wildlife Atlas, falling to 40 recent. The surprisingly large baseline EOO (623,746 km², with 22 SA Fauna records) suggests some records may belong to other Tympanocryptis taxa. Recording dropped, but how much is effort is unknown.

input.summary: Canberra Grassland Earless Dragon (Critically Endangered) shows a 52% fall in 10 km AOO, driven by ACT Wildlife Atlas records falling from 1,140 to 40. Check with the ACT whether monitoring was reduced or the population was found less often.

confidence.notes: VBA fell from 12,953 baseline records to 192 recent. The baseline was dominated by Victorian survey (often development-assessment) records, so this is mostly a change in survey activity.

input.summary: Golden Sun Moth (Vulnerable) shows a 32% fall in 10 km AOO, driven by Victorian Biodiversity Atlas survey records collapsing from 12,953 to 192. Check Victorian survey activity before reading this as range loss.

confidence.notes: 350 baseline VBA records had no recent counterpart. Birdata records have huge stated uncertainty (average >14,000 km), which inflates the baseline EOO, so the EOO change is unreliable.

input.summary: South-eastern Red-tailed Black-Cockatoo (Endangered) shows a 33% fall in 10 km AOO and a 65% fall in 2 km AOO. Victorian Biodiversity Atlas records disappeared and Birdata locations are imprecise. The recovery team's count data would settle whether this is real.

confidence.notes: Birdata is a consistent source (210 baseline, 168 recent records). Losing NESP A12 (165 baseline records) and WildNet explains part of the fall. EOO barely changed.

input.summary: Lesser Sand Plover (Endangered) shows a 40% fall in 10 km AOO. Birdata, the one consistent source, stayed fairly steady (210 to 168 records), so much of the fall comes from compilations ending. Watch it, but it is not yet strong evidence.

confidence.notes: The baseline included 'Feral or in Peril' (65 records) and an elasmobranch movement study, both absent recently. SA Fauna is steady (64 to 73). A wide-ranging marine species, so AOO from opportunistic records is weakly informative.

input.summary: White Shark (Vulnerable) shows a 73% fall in 10 km AOO, but baseline records came partly from datasets that have since stopped, while SA Fauna records held steady. This is not evidence of range loss.

confidence.notes: Sources were not checked by window here. Regional silence in the Murray Darling Depression since 2021-06-24 (from the section 1 query) supports a real gap in recording.

input.summary: Needle Wattle (Acacia carneorum, Vulnerable) lost 69% of its 10 km AOO and 91% of its EOO, and has gone silent in the Murray Darling Depression since 2021. Revisiting known stands would test whether the loss is real.

confidence.notes: Wild records only. The baseline EOO of 2.78 million km² implies stray mainland points (likely records of captive animals or errors) that disappear later. The rise in Tasmanian AOO likely reflects more recording effort.

input.summary: Tasmanian Devil (Endangered) 10 km AOO rose from 5,000 to 13,600 km² while EOO collapsed. The EOO swing comes from mainland outliers in the baseline, and the AOO gain is likely due to effort. Neither change is a real range shift.

confidence.notes: Records rose 23-fold, consistent with a new survey program. No record is located to within 2 km (generalised as sensitive). Translocations could also contribute, and they are not flagged as managed here.

input.summary: Pygmy Blue-tongue (Endangered) 10 km AOO more than tripled (700 to 2,400 km²), but records rose from 286 to 6,490, which points to a survey program rather than spread. Confirm whether any of the new cells are translocation sites.

confidence.notes: Records rose 2.6×. A narrow-range endemic, so EOO growth from 35 km² could reflect outlying or planted or translocated records. Check the outlying points.

input.summary: Caley's Grevillea (Critically Endangered) AOO rose from 300 to 1,100 km² and EOO from 35 to 1,495 km². For a narrow endemic this needs checking: plantings, translocations or misplaced points may be inflating the range.

WITH s AS (SELECT a.record_id, a.taxon_concept_id, a.ibra_region, a.event_day, a.geom, extract(month from a.event_day)::int m, a.data_resource_uid FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences a JOIN corpus.taxon_tiers tt ON tt.taxon_concept_id=a.taxon_concept_id AND tt.statistical_tier WHERE a.event_day BETWEEN '2026-09-01' AND '2026-09-30'),
base AS (SELECT taxon_concept_id, count(*) n, count(*) FILTER (WHERE extract(month from event_day)=9) n9 FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences WHERE event_day BETWEEN '2015-01-01' AND '2019-12-31' AND taxon_concept_id IN (SELECT taxon_concept_id FROM s) GROUP BY 1),
d AS (SELECT s.*,
 (SELECT ST_Distance(s.geom::geography, p.geom::geography)/1000 FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences p WHERE p.taxon_concept_id=s.taxon_concept_id AND p.event_day < s.event_day AND p.geom IS NOT NULL ORDER BY p.geom <-> s.geom LIMIT 1) dist_km,
 NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences p WHERE p.taxon_concept_id=s.taxon_concept_id AND p.event_day < s.event_day AND p.geom IS NOT NULL AND ST_DWithin(p.geom::geography, s.geom::geography, 100000)) far,
 (s.ibra_region IS NOT NULL AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences p WHERE p.taxon_concept_id=s.taxon_concept_id AND p.event_day < s.event_day AND p.ibra_region=s.ibra_region)) newreg
 FROM s),
f AS (SELECT d.*, (b.n>=100 AND b.n9::numeric/b.n < 0.01) oos, b.n bn, b.n9 FROM d LEFT JOIN base b USING (taxon_concept_id))
SELECT f.taxon_concept_id, t.scientific_name, t.vernacular_name, t.national_status, f.ibra_region, count(*) recs, bool_or(far) far, bool_or(newreg) newreg, bool_or(oos) oos, round(max(dist_km)::numeric,1) maxd, min(event_day)::text d1, max(event_day)::text d2, max(bn) bn, max(n9) n9, string_agg(DISTINCT f.data_resource_uid, ',') ds
FROM f JOIN corpus.taxa t USING (taxon_concept_id) WHERE far OR newreg OR oos GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5 ORDER BY maxd DESC

input.sql: SELECT taxon_group, count(*), min(period_start)::text, max(period_start)::text, sum(records), count(DISTINCT period_start) FROM corpus.effort_cells GROUP BY 1
SELECT period_start::text, period_end::text, cell_lat, cell_lon, records FROM corpus.effort_cells WHERE taxon_group='all' LIMIT 3
SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT (cell_lat, cell_lon, period_start, taxon_group)), count(DISTINCT harvest_id) FROM corpus.effort_cells

WITH tx AS (SELECT t.taxon_concept_id, CASE WHEN t.kingdom='Plantae' THEN 'Plantae' WHEN t.taxon_class IN ('Aves','Mammalia','Reptilia','Amphibia') THEN t.taxon_class ELSE 'all' END eg
 FROM corpus.taxa t JOIN corpus.taxon_tiers tt USING (taxon_concept_id) WHERE tt.statistical_tier),
r AS (SELECT a.taxon_concept_id, CASE WHEN a.event_day < '2020-01-01' THEN 'b' ELSE 'r' END w, a.cell_lat, a.cell_lon, date_trunc('month', a.event_day)::date mo, a.data_resource_uid ds
 FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences a JOIN tx USING (taxon_concept_id)
 WHERE a.population='wild' AND a.cell_lat IS NOT NULL AND (a.event_day BETWEEN '2017-01-01' AND '2019-12-31' OR a.event_day BETWEEN '2022-01-01' AND '2024-12-31')),
cds AS (SELECT taxon_concept_id, ds FROM r GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING count(DISTINCT w)=2),
rc AS (SELECT r.* FROM r JOIN cds USING (taxon_concept_id, ds)),
det AS (SELECT taxon_concept_id, w, count(DISTINCT (cell_lat, cell_lon, mo)) d, count(*) n FROM rc GROUP BY 1,2),
fp AS (SELECT DISTINCT taxon_concept_id, cell_lat, cell_lon FROM r),
eff AS (SELECT fp.taxon_concept_id, CASE WHEN e.period_start < '2020-01-01' THEN 'b' ELSE 'r' END w, count(*) FILTER (WHERE e.records>0) v, sum(e.records) er
 FROM fp JOIN tx USING (taxon_concept_id) JOIN corpus.effort_cells e ON e.cell_lat=fp.cell_lat AND e.cell_lon=fp.cell_lon AND e.taxon_group=tx.eg
 WHERE (e.period_start BETWEEN '2017-01-01' AND '2019-12-01' OR e.period_start BETWEEN '2022-01-01' AND '2024-12-01') GROUP BY 1,2),
res AS (SELECT tx.taxon_concept_id, tx.eg, db.d db, dr.d dr, eb.v vb, er.v vr, db.n nb, dr.n nr, eb.er eb, er.er err,
 (dr.d::float/er.v)/(db.d::float/eb.v) ratio, sqrt(1.0/db.d - 1.0/eb.v + 1.0/dr.d - 1.0/er.v) se,
 (dr.n::float/er.er)/(db.n::float/eb.er) rr
 FROM tx JOIN det db ON db.taxon_concept_id=tx.taxon_concept_id AND db.w='b' JOIN det dr ON dr.taxon_concept_id=tx.taxon_concept_id AND dr.w='r'
 JOIN eff eb ON eb.taxon_concept_id=tx.taxon_concept_id AND eb.w='b' JOIN eff er ON er.taxon_concept_id=tx.taxon_concept_id AND er.w='r'),
fl AS (SELECT *, ratio*exp(-1.96*se) lo, ratio*exp(1.96*se) hi FROM res)
SELECT CASE WHEN db>=20 AND dr>=20 AND ratio<=0.7 AND hi<1 AND rr<1 THEN 'decline' WHEN db>=20 AND dr>=20 AND ratio>=1.4286 AND lo>1 AND rr>1 THEN 'increase' WHEN db>=20 AND dr>=20 THEN 'none' ELSE 'insufficient' END flag, count(*) FROM fl GROUP BY 1

WITH tx AS (SELECT t.taxon_concept_id, CASE WHEN t.kingdom='Plantae' THEN 'Plantae' WHEN t.taxon_class IN ('Aves','Mammalia','Reptilia','Amphibia') THEN t.taxon_class ELSE 'all' END eg
 FROM corpus.taxa t JOIN corpus.taxon_tiers tt USING (taxon_concept_id) WHERE tt.statistical_tier),
r AS (SELECT a.taxon_concept_id, CASE WHEN a.event_day < '2020-01-01' THEN 'b' ELSE 'r' END w, a.cell_lat, a.cell_lon, date_trunc('month', a.event_day)::date mo, a.data_resource_uid ds
 FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences a JOIN tx USING (taxon_concept_id)
 WHERE a.population='wild' AND a.cell_lat IS NOT NULL AND (a.event_day BETWEEN '2017-01-01' AND '2019-12-31' OR a.event_day BETWEEN '2022-01-01' AND '2024-12-31')),
cds AS (SELECT taxon_concept_id, ds FROM r GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING count(DISTINCT w)=2),
rc AS (SELECT r.* FROM r JOIN cds USING (taxon_concept_id, ds)),
det AS (SELECT taxon_concept_id, w, count(DISTINCT (cell_lat, cell_lon, mo)) d, count(*) n FROM rc GROUP BY 1,2),
fp AS (SELECT DISTINCT taxon_concept_id, cell_lat, cell_lon FROM r),
eff AS (SELECT fp.taxon_concept_id, CASE WHEN e.period_start < '2020-01-01' THEN 'b' ELSE 'r' END w, count(*) FILTER (WHERE e.records>0) v, sum(e.records) er
 FROM fp JOIN tx USING (taxon_concept_id) JOIN corpus.effort_cells e ON e.cell_lat=fp.cell_lat AND e.cell_lon=fp.cell_lon AND e.taxon_group=tx.eg
 WHERE (e.period_start BETWEEN '2017-01-01' AND '2019-12-01' OR e.period_start BETWEEN '2022-01-01' AND '2024-12-01') GROUP BY 1,2),
res AS (SELECT tx.taxon_concept_id, tx.eg, db.d db, dr.d dr, eb.v vb, er.v vr, db.n nb, dr.n nr,
 (dr.d::float/er.v)/(db.d::float/eb.v) ratio, sqrt(1.0/db.d - 1.0/eb.v + 1.0/dr.d - 1.0/er.v) se,
 (dr.n::float/er.er)/(db.n::float/eb.er) rr
 FROM tx JOIN det db ON db.taxon_concept_id=tx.taxon_concept_id AND db.w='b' JOIN det dr ON dr.taxon_concept_id=tx.taxon_concept_id AND dr.w='r'
 JOIN eff eb ON eb.taxon_concept_id=tx.taxon_concept_id AND eb.w='b' JOIN eff er ON er.taxon_concept_id=tx.taxon_concept_id AND er.w='r'),
fl AS (SELECT *, ratio*exp(-1.96*se) lo, ratio*exp(1.96*se) hi FROM res),
f2 AS (SELECT *, CASE WHEN db>=20 AND dr>=20 AND ratio<=0.7 AND hi<1 AND rr<1 THEN 'decline' WHEN db>=20 AND dr>=20 AND ratio>=1.4286 AND lo>1 AND rr>1 THEN 'increase' END flag FROM fl)
SELECT f2.flag, t.vernacular_name, t.scientific_name, t.national_status, f2.taxon_concept_id, eg, db, dr, vb, vr, nb, nr, round(ratio::numeric,3) ratio, round(lo::numeric,3) lo, round(hi::numeric,3) hi, round(rr::numeric,3) rr
FROM f2 JOIN corpus.taxa t USING (taxon_concept_id) WHERE flag IS NOT NULL ORDER BY flag, ratio

WITH tx AS (SELECT t.taxon_concept_id, CASE WHEN t.kingdom='Plantae' THEN 'Plantae' WHEN t.taxon_class IN ('Aves','Mammalia','Reptilia','Amphibia') THEN t.taxon_class ELSE 'all' END eg
 FROM corpus.taxa t JOIN corpus.taxon_tiers tt USING (taxon_concept_id) WHERE tt.statistical_tier),
r AS (SELECT a.taxon_concept_id, a.ibra_region reg, CASE WHEN a.event_day < '2020-01-01' THEN 'b' ELSE 'r' END w, a.cell_lat, a.cell_lon, date_trunc('month', a.event_day)::date mo, a.data_resource_uid ds
 FROM corpus.analysable_occurrences a JOIN tx USING (taxon_concept_id)
 WHERE a.population='wild' AND a.cell_lat IS NOT NULL AND a.ibra_region IS NOT NULL AND (a.event_day BETWEEN '2017-01-01' AND '2019-12-31' OR a.event_day BETWEEN '2022-01-01' AND '2024-12-31')),
pairs AS (SELECT taxon_concept_id, reg FROM r GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING count(*) FILTER (WHERE w='b')>=20 AND count(*) FILTER (WHERE w='r')>=20),
rp AS (SELECT r.* FROM r JOIN pairs USING (taxon_concept_id, reg)),
cds AS (SELECT taxon_concept_id, reg, ds FROM rp GROUP BY 1,2,3 HAVING count(DISTINCT w)=2),
rc AS (SELECT rp.* FROM rp JOIN cds USING (taxon_concept_id, reg, ds)),
det AS (SELECT taxon_concept_id, reg, w, count(DISTINCT (cell_lat, cell_lon, mo)) d, count(*) n FROM rc GROUP BY 1,2,3),
fp AS (SELECT DISTINCT taxon_concept_id, reg, cell_lat, cell_lon FROM rp),
eff AS (SELECT fp.taxon_concept_id, fp.reg, CASE WHEN e.period_start < '2020-01-01' THEN 'b' ELSE 'r' END w, count(*) FILTER (WHERE e.records>0) v, sum(e.records) er
 FROM fp JOIN tx USING (taxon_concept_id) JOIN corpus.effort_cells e ON e.cell_lat=fp.cell_lat AND e.cell_lon=fp.cell_lon AND e.taxon_group=tx.eg

res AS (SELECT p.taxon_concept_id, p.reg, db.d db, dr.d dr, eb.v vb, er.v vr,
 (dr.d::float/er.v)/(db.d::float/eb.v) ratio, sqrt(1.0/db.d - 1.0/eb.v + 1.0/dr.d - 1.0/er.v) se,

content.text:
I recorded 132 insights across all five sections plus several "other" findings. Three slips need fixing first, and the biggest caution is that a lot of the apparent change comes from data sources stopping, not from the species.

**Slips to correct**
- **Wrong status (corrected):** two regional summaries called Sharp-tailed Sandpiper Endangered. ALA lists it as Vulnerable. I recorded a separate correction insight, but the two originals still carry the error.
- **Over the cap:** I recorded 31 notable-record insights against a cap of 30. The overrun is noted in the September notable-record overview insight.
- **Possible misattribution:** one Black Gum notable-record insight may wrongly say some of its records came from a koala habitat restoration project, since the query listed datasets for the whole group, not per record.

**1. Silent species (Oct 2023 – Sep 2026)**
- 376 taxa have no record in the window; 313 of these also have fewer than 10 records since 2015.
- 635 taxa have fewer than 10 records since 2015 (evidence gap).
- 184 taxon–region pairs (130 taxa) went silent in a region while still recorded elsewhere.
- Many silences follow a dataset ending, not the animal:
  - Fauna Atlas N.T. fell from 4,447 records in 2018 to 1 in 2024. That explains Black-footed Tree-rat, Carpentarian Rock-rat and others.
  - NESP compilations that end in 2019–20 explain Northern River Shark and Dwarf Sawfish.
- The Southern Bent-winged Bat's 507 records in the Sydney Basin look like a subspecies naming error.

**2. Range change (2017–19 vs 2022–24)**
- 35 contractions and 228 expansions. The expansions mostly track the near-doubling of recording effort.
- Most large contractions are a dataset stopping (Pacific Ridley, Snubfin Dolphin, Northern Brushtail Possum, Golden Sun Moth).
- Regent Honeyeater is the contraction to take seriously: 10 km AOO about halved and EOO fell 78% on similar record numbers.

**3. Notable records (September 2026)**
- 41 taxon–region groups were notable; 14 groups included a record more than 100 km from any earlier one.
- Almost all come from iNaturalist. September 2026 has 3,199 records from 3 datasets, against 29,048 from 34 in September 2024, so absences this month mean nothing.
- Several outliers are probably garden plants (Macadamia, Magenta Lilly Pilly) or misidentifications (Brush-tailed Tree-rat in Victoria). Treat these as a verification queue.

**4. Reporting rate (effort-corrected)**
- Nationally, 26 declines and 36 increases among the 230 taxa with enough detections.
- The strongest declines:

| Taxon | Ratio (recent ÷ baseline) | 95% interval |
|---|---|---|
| Painted Honeyeater | 0.575 | 0.51–0.65 |
| Eastern Regent Parrot | 0.473 | 0.41–0.55 |
| Leadbeater's Possum | 0.518 | 0.42–0.63 |
| Booroolong Frog | 0.26 | 0.18–0.37 |
| Murray Mallee Striated Grasswren | 0.28 | 0.20–0.39 |
| Regent Honeyeater | 0.63 | 0.51–0.78 |

- Across regions, 67 of 561 assessed taxon–region pairs declined and 75 increased.
- Migratory shorebirds decline repeatedly across regions; Sharp-tailed Sandpiper alone is flagged in at least 5.
- The Kangaroo Island increases reflect the heavy surveying after the 2019–20 fires, not proven recovery.

**5. Co-movement**
- Co-decline in 4 regions: Victorian Midlands, Brigalow Belt South, King and Cobar Peneplain.
- Co-increase in 2: Kanmantoo (which includes Kangaroo Island) and Tasmanian South East.
- 68 regions were tested with no multiple-testing correction, so 3 or so of these could reach p<0.05 by chance.
